summary.id: Lapisan es tipis yang menyelimuti rumput dan tanaman di Dataran Tinggi Dieng pada malam kemarau yang cerah dan dingin; warga menyebutnya “embun racun” karena dapat mematikan tanaman kentang.
summary.en: A thin layer of ice on grass and crops on the Dieng Plateau on clear, cold dry-season nights; locals call it “poison dew” because it can kill potato plants.

scientific.id: Bun upas (juga ditulis embun upas) adalah lapisan es tipis yang menutupi rumput, daun, dan tanaman di Dataran Tinggi Dieng pada malam musim kemarau yang cerah. Menurut BMKG, penduduk Dieng mengartikan namanya sebagai “embun racun”, karena es itu menyelimuti tanaman kentang dan mematikannya; BMKG juga menyebutnya embun es, yang kadang disangka salju. BMKG menyebut gerak semu matahari, masuknya udara dingin, dan laju penurunan suhu terhadap ketinggian sebagai faktor di balik cuaca dingin yang mendahuluinya, tanpa merincinya, dan menyebut suhu dingin seperti ini umum terjadi pada bulan-bulan puncak kemarau, Juli sampai September. Penjelasan BMKG: pada musim itu awan dan hujan berkurang, sehingga energi yang dilepas bumi pada malam hari tidak tertahan dan lolos ke luar angkasa, dan udara dekat permukaan mendingin dari malam hingga pagi. Angin timur dari Australia yang sedang musim dingin, disebut BMKG monsun dingin Australia, ikut membawa udara yang lebih dingin ke Jawa. Rujukan umum tentang embun beku radiasi (FAO dan materi pelatihan NWS) menambahkan mekanismenya: pada malam cerah dan tenang, rumput dan tanah melepas panas lebih cepat daripada yang mereka terima, sehingga udara paling dingin berada tepat di atas permukaan dan suhu naik seiring ketinggian (inversi permukaan). Bila permukaan mencapai titik beku, uap air dapat langsung menjadi es (embun beku, hoar), atau embun yang sudah terbentuk membeku. Awan dan angin melemahkan proses ini, dan permukaan tanah bisa lebih dingin daripada suhu yang dicatat termometer standar pada ketinggian sekitar 1,25–2 m, sehingga es dapat muncul walau pembacaan resmi masih di atas nol. Sebuah laporan BMKG tentang seminar ilmiah di Banjarnegara (2023) menyebut embun es muncul terutama pada musim kemarau, sekitar Juni sampai Oktober, menjelaskannya sebagai embun yang membeku pada udara yang sangat dingin, dan mencatat bahwa pengamatan dengan stasiun cuaca otomatis di kawasan Candi Arjuna berjalan sejak 2020. Satu-satunya studi berbasis pengamatan di Dieng yang sudah kami baca, Kurniawan dan Kristianto (2026), memakai data stasiun cuaca otomatis 10 menitan (sekitar 2.050 m) selama 2021–2025 dan membandingkan 50 malam yang tercatat berembun beku dengan 1.769 malam lainnya. Tanggal kejadian diambil dari laporan resmi, media, dan dokumentasi bergambar, bukan dari sensor. Embun beku tercatat pada sekitar 2,75 % malam: 26 dari 50 pada Juli, 11 pada Agustus, dan 6 pada Juni. Pada malam-malam itu median suhu udara minimum adalah 2,65 °C (11,36 °C pada malam lain) dan median kecepatan angin rata-rata 0,33 m/s (1,17 m/s), dengan sinyal hujan malam yang lebih rendah; kelembapan relatif dan selisih titik embun tidak berbeda nyata, karena udara di sana lembap hampir setiap malam. Penulis menyimpulkan bahwa embun beku Dieng lebih tepat dipahami sebagai malam yang dingin, tenang, dan sesuai dengan pelepasan panas yang efisien pada musim kering, bukan sekadar suhu rendah.
scientific.en: Bun upas (also written embun upas) is a thin layer of ice that covers grass, leaves and crops on the Dieng Plateau on clear dry-season nights. According to BMKG, Dieng residents take the name to mean “poison dew”, because the ice coats potato plants and kills them; BMKG also calls it ice dew, which some people mistake for snow. BMKG names the apparent motion of the sun, intrusions of cold air and the rate at which temperature falls with height as factors behind the cold weather that precedes it, without detailing them, and says such cold is common in the peak months of the dry season, July to September. BMKG's explanation: in that season clouds and rain are fewer, so the energy the earth gives off at night is not held back and escapes to space, and the air near the surface cools from night into morning. Easterly winds from Australia in its winter, called the Australian cold monsoon by BMKG, also bring cooler air to Java. General references on radiation frost (FAO and an NWS training page) add the mechanism: on a clear, calm night grass and soil lose heat faster than they receive it, so the coldest air lies right above the surface and temperature rises with height (a surface inversion). If the surface reaches freezing, water vapour can turn straight into ice (hoar frost), or dew that has already formed can freeze. Cloud and wind weaken the process, and the ground surface can be colder than the temperature logged by a standard thermometer at about 1.25–2 m, so ice can appear while the official reading is still above zero. A BMKG report on a scientific seminar in Banjarnegara (2023) says ice dew appears mainly in the dry season, about June to October, describes it as dew freezing in very cold air, and notes that observations with an automatic weather station near the Arjuna temple complex have run since 2020. The only observation-based Dieng study we have read, Kurniawan and Kristianto (2026), used 10-minute automatic weather station data (about 2,050 m) for 2021–2025 and compared 50 nights documented as frost nights with 1,769 other nights. The event dates came from official reports, media and dated photos, not from a sensor. Frost was recorded on about 2.75 % of nights: 26 of the 50 in July, 11 in August and 6 in June. On those nights the median minimum air temperature was 2.65 °C (11.36 °C on other nights) and the median mean wind speed 0.33 m/s (1.17 m/s), with a lower night-time rainfall signal; relative humidity and dew-point depression did not differ significantly, because the air there is humid almost every night. The authors conclude that Dieng frost is better understood as a cold, calm night consistent with efficient heat loss in the dry season than as low temperature alone.

caveat.id: Artikel BMKG (2021) hanya menyebut faktor-faktor pendahulu tanpa rincian. Mekanisme pendinginan radiasi dan pembentukan es berasal dari rujukan umum tentang embun beku radiasi (FAO; materi pelatihan NWS). Studi Dieng (Kurniawan dan Kristianto, 2026) sesuai dengan mekanisme itu, tetapi datanya tidak mencakup tutupan awan, radiasi gelombang panjang, atau suhu permukaan daun dan tanah, sehingga tidak membuktikannya secara langsung. Tanggal kejadiannya berasal dari laporan dokumenter dan tinggi sensor suhu tidak dilaporkan. Angka 2,65 °C adalah median suhu udara minimum di stasiun, bukan suhu permukaan rumput, dan artikel tidak menyebut berapa malam yang minimumnya di bawah nol.
caveat.en: The BMKG article (2021) only names the preceding factors without detail. The radiative-cooling and ice-formation mechanism comes from general references on radiation frost (FAO; an NWS training page). The Dieng study (Kurniawan and Kristianto, 2026) is consistent with it, but its data include no cloud cover, longwave radiation, or leaf or soil surface temperature, so it does not prove the mechanism directly. Its event dates come from documentary reports and the temperature sensor height is not reported. The 2.65 °C figure is the median of the station's nightly minimum air temperature, not a grass-surface temperature, and the article does not say how many nights had a minimum below zero.

curator_notes: NEW: Kurniawan & Kristianto (2026), Buletin Fisika 28(1), supplied by you. I read the full PDF text myself (pdftotext), so the figures on the page are checked against it: 2,050 m AWS at 7°12'18"S 109°54'27"E; 2021-2025; 1,819 nights, 50 frost nights (2.75%); July 26, Aug 11, Jun 6; median min temperature 2.65 vs 11.36 C; wind 0.33 vs 1.17 m/s; RH and dew-point depression not different. The pin now sits at that AWS. Oddity: the issue is dated February 2026 but the paper says accepted 27 August 2026; no DOI shown, licence not shown, so I only paraphrase.

The paper's own limits are carried into the public Note: dates come from documentary reports (25 explicit/official or dated-visual, 22 retrospective or multi-day, 3 lower-confidence), no cloud/longwave/surface-temperature data, sensor height unknown. It does NOT say how many frost nights had a minimum below 0 C, so the page gives no 'below zero' figure.

The other three sources (BMKG 2021, FAO ch.1, NWS training page) were read through a fetch agent's account, not verbatim. Please skim them: BMKG (the three factors, 'Juli-September', clear-sky wording, Australian monsoon quote); FAO (inversion top 9-60 m, hoar frost vs frozen dew, frost defined at 1.25-2 m); NWS (ground colder than the screen; the page itself says frost is not frozen dew in one answer and allows frozen dew in another).

The NWS training page is by Jeff Haby, publisher inferred from the URL; it is a training page, not a journal article. A better general citation (Met Office, WMO, or a book the paper cites: Snyder & Melo-Abreu 2005 is the FAO volume already used; Kalma et al. 1992) would help.
